text.p: Thai Foreign Minister Amnuay Viravan on Wednesday applauded President Bill Clinton's re-election and said he hoped it would help consolidate a stronger U.S. role in Asia.
He said Clinton was showing signs of putting more importance on American-Asian ties, and said he hoped upcoming trips to the region would help cement the U.S. vow to play a strong role in Asia.
"Certainly we want to see closer relations. Especially we would like to see the United States come to play a key role in this region, we do not want them to pull back," Amnuay said.

"We need to have a balance of power in the region. In Asia there are countries with a lot of power -- Japan plays a prominent economic role while China plays a major role in security and politics," he said.
"We want the United States to play a major role in this region so a small country like Thailand can benefit," he said.
Clinton's re-election will also help maintain continuity, Amnuay said.
Thailand is due to sign a tax treaty with the United States later this month when Clinton visits Bangkok on November 25.
